whatChanged.headline: Meta Says Its AI Is Getting Better at Remembering You. What Does That Mean?
whatChanged.headlineZh: Meta 让 AI 更会记住你，这意味着什么？
intro: On 6 November, Meta said it was rolling out specialized versions of its existing models, trained using Muse Wonder, to Muse and Meta AI. The company highlighted two features: Active Memory, which identifies useful details from earlier conversations, and Active Focus, designed to help an assistant stay on track with a user's goals.

The announcement is about a shift in how assistants work, not just a bigger model. A chatbot that remembers yesterday's constraints may be more useful today. But it also raises a practical question: which details should an AI keep?
introZh: 2026 年 11 月 6 日，Meta 宣布将基于 Muse Wonder 训练的专门模型逐步引入 Muse 和 Meta AI。它重点介绍两项能力：Active Memory 可以识别过去对话中值得记住的信息；Active Focus 则帮助助手围绕用户的目标持续开展工作。
这不只是一次模型升级。过去的聊天机器人往往需要你反复解释背景；更有记忆力的助手可以接着上次的事情往下做。但一个新问题也随之出现：什么值得 AI 记住，什么应该被放下？

sections.heading: What is actually changing?
paragraphs: Meta says the specialized models are trained using its larger Muse Wonder system and are being rolled out to users of Muse and Meta AI. The company describes Active Memory as distinguishing temporary details from durable ones, recognizing when old context becomes relevant, and noticing when information is stale. Active Focus is meant to support longer tasks and changing instructions.

Think of planning a trip. A helpful assistant might remember that you prefer trains over flights, while treating last Tuesday's restaurant booking as temporary. The useful part is not retaining everything. It is knowing which context matters for the next decision.
paragraphsZh: Meta 表示，新模型由 Muse Wonder 的能力训练而来，正逐步应用于 Muse 和 Meta AI。按照公司的介绍，Active Memory 不只是保存聊天记录，还要判断哪些信息是临时的、哪些可能长期有用，以及旧信息什么时候已经过时。Active Focus 则帮助助手处理持续性任务，并适应用户中途改变的要求。
比如规划旅行。一个真正有用的助手可以记住你更喜欢坐火车，而不是每次重新问；但上周二订过哪家餐厅，不一定需要长期保存。关键不在于记住所有事情，而在于知道下一次决策需要哪些背景。

sections.heading: How much better does Meta say it is?
sections.headingZh: Meta 公布的成绩提升了多少？
paragraphs: Meta reports a score of 47% for its current Muse model on its Personal Superintelligence Index, compared with 38% for the previous model. On an Active Memory evaluation, it reports 90% of tasks correctly using critical context, versus 76% previously. It also says the improved models in Muse show a 2.4-times reduction in forgetting critical information.

Those numbers come from Meta's own evaluations. They do not establish that an assistant will remember 90% of everything you tell it, or that all users already have access to every feature. The announcement does not provide enough independent testing to judge how reliably the system handles sensitive or outdated personal details.
paragraphsZh: 在 Meta 自己的 Personal Superintelligence Index 评估中，当前 Muse 模型得分为 47%，上一版本为 38%。在 Active Memory 测试中，正确使用关键上下文的任务比例由 76% 升至 90%。Meta 还称，Muse 中的新模型遗忘重要信息的情况减少了约 2.4 倍。
这些都是 Meta 公布的内部评估，不代表 AI 能记住用户说过的 90% 的事情，也不能据此判断每个人已经用上所有功能。对于敏感信息、过期信息究竟处理得如何，目前还缺少充分的独立测试。

sections.heading: Why does memory matter more than another clever answer?
sections.headingZh: 为什么记忆可能比更聪明的回答重要？
paragraphs: For many everyday tasks, the frustrating part of AI is not a lack of intelligence. It is the need to restate preferences, explain earlier decisions and correct forgotten constraints. Better continuity could make assistants useful for projects that last weeks rather than minutes.

The trade-off is that a remembered detail can become wrong. A food preference, job search or travel plan may change. An assistant needs a way to use context without turning an old statement into a permanent label. Users should check the available memory and privacy controls in the products they use rather than assume all assistants work the same way.
paragraphsZh: 很多人使用 AI 的麻烦，不是它答不出问题，而是每次都要重新交代背景：我不喜欢什么、之前决定了什么、项目进行到哪一步。更好的连续性，可能让 AI 从回答单个问题，变成真正协助完成几周甚至几个月的工作。
但记忆也有风险。一个人以前的饮食习惯、求职方向或者旅行计划，都可能改变。如果 AI 把过去一句话当成永久标签，就会越帮越错。使用这类产品时，最好查看它实际提供哪些记忆和隐私控制，而不是假设所有助手都采用相同规则。

whatChanged.ending: The next test for personal AI may be not how much it can remember, but how well it knows when to forget.
whatChanged.endingZh: 个人 AI 的下一场考试，或许不是能记住多少，而是懂不懂什么时候该忘记。

stayCurious.headline: Why Does Singapore Have a Walkway Called the Five-Foot Way?
stayCurious.headlineZh: 新加坡的“五脚基”，为什么叫这个名字？
intro: Walk past a row of old shophouses in Singapore and you may notice a narrow covered corridor running from one storefront to the next. It is called the five-foot way, or wu jiao ji in Chinese.
This small detail reveals how colonial planning made space for public passage.
introZh: 走过新加坡的老店屋，你会发现一条有屋顶的走廊，从一家店门口延伸到下一家。华人通常叫它“五脚基”，英文是 five-foot way。
这条小走廊，体现了早期城市规划如何为公众留出通道。

sections.heading: Where did the idea come from?
sections.headingZh: 五脚基最早是怎么来的？
paragraphs: Singapore's National Heritage Board traces the covered verandah requirement to Stamford Raffles. On 4 November 1822, he issued building stipulations calling for a verandah of a certain depth that would remain open as a continuous covered passage along the street.

The five-foot way became a shophouse hallmark. Shophouses appeared in the town centre in the 1840s and later spread elsewhere. The name describes a traditional dimension, but it should not be taken as a guarantee that every surviving corridor measures exactly five feet today.
paragraphsZh: 新加坡国家文物局的资料将这种连续骑楼走廊的规定追溯到莱佛士。1822 年 11 月 4 日，他提出建筑要求：房屋沿街必须留出一定深度的走廊，并保持相连、供行人通行。
五脚基后来成为店屋的典型特征。店屋从 1840 年代起出现在市中心，随后扩展到其他街区。虽然英文名字直译是“五英尺走道”，但不能据此认为今天每一条老走廊都精确宽五英尺。

sections.heading: Why build a corridor under someone else's upstairs room?
sections.headingZh: 为什么要把走廊建在别人家的楼下？
paragraphs: The column-supported upper floor shelters a continuous pedestrian route from sun and rain.

The Urban Redevelopment Authority describes the five-foot way as a continuous colonnaded walkway and an important part of the experience of historic conservation areas. Tiles, columns, shopfronts and ceilings also shape its character.
paragraphsZh: 店屋二楼向街道伸出，由柱子支撑，下面形成连续的遮阳挡雨通道。
市区重建局 URA 将五脚基视为历史保护区的重要组成部分。值得保留的不只是屋檐，还有地砖、柱廊、店面和天花板。这些细节共同构成了老街的步行体验。

sections.heading: Can owners change it however they like?
sections.headingZh: 店主可以随意装修五脚基吗？
paragraphs: Not in conserved areas. URA's conservation guidance requires retaining original granite edging and encourages traditional floor finishes. It also addresses mismatched floor levels between neighbouring units, recommending appropriate ramps in certain circumstances.
Different tiles and floor levels reflect buildings owned and restored separately.
paragraphsZh: 在受保护的历史街区，不可以完全随意。URA 的修复指引要求保留原有花岗岩边条，并鼓励保留传统地面饰材；相邻店屋地面高低不一致时，也有相应的坡道和修复要求。
因此，连成一体的走廊也会有不同地砖和高差，反映各店屋不同的业主与修复历史。

stayCurious.ending: The next time rain sends you under a shophouse arcade, notice how a small planning rule from two centuries ago still shapes an ordinary walk.
stayCurious.endingZh: 下次下雨躲进五脚基时，不妨想想：两百多年前的一条建筑规定，今天仍在影响我们怎么走路。
